module: D09-14 Market Share／Entry Barrier／Substitution／Competitive Strategy市占、進入障礙、替代與競爭策略

theorySources.use: Market share/concentration require correct market definition and corroborating competition evidence.
Entry barriers include structural, strategic and network/switching mechanisms.
Market shares can be measured using different metrics; recent/foreseeable changes can make historical shares over/understate competitive significance.
Product and geographic market definition precedes meaningful market-share interpretation.

marketShareContract.rule: Do not compare shares built from different numerators/denominators as if interchangeable.
marketShareContract.vintage: Every share requires observationPeriod, sourcePublishedAt/capturedAt and market-definition vintage.

mechanisms: Durable share can indicate competitive advantage only when the relevant market is correctly defined and share survives entry/substitution pressure.
High qualification costs and yield/process learning can delay entry even when capital is available.
Substitution risk can convert a high-share incumbent into a shrinking economic market; share within an obsolete denominator is misleading.
falsification: Historical market share can overstate future significance after technology, capacity, regulation or customer-sourcing changes.
A high-share firm can destroy value through overinvestment, price wars or poor capital allocation.
A low-share challenger can exert strong competitive pressure if it has credible rapid-entry or swing-capacity capability.
Reported 'market share' from sell-side or company presentations is unusable unless product/geography/period/denominator are explicit.
Capex size alone is not an entry barrier if capacity can be leased, outsourced or rapidly repurposed.

pitContract.missingRule: UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN; do not infer zero share or no substitute.
pitContract.outcomeFirewall: No future return/margin outcome when freezing share/barrier/substitution states.

redundancyControls: Share/concentration is not a duplicate vote with D09-10 HHI/activity concentration.
Entry barriers must be separated from current pricing power and current margins.
Substitution evidence must not be duplicated with theme/industry classification bridges.
